To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the rate of reaction of ozone with a double bond in a fatty acid depends on the location of the double bond in the micelle, the concentration of the fatty acid, and the rate of diffusion of the ozone to the double bond.

ozone reacts with unsaturated fatty acids, and not with tryptophan, when the fatty acids are present in reverse micelles with the protein lysozyme; and that the location of unsaturated fatty acids at the micellar-water interface, or in the bulk organic phase, has no effect on the rate of reaction with ozone.

ozone reacts with olefinic compounds at the micelle-water interface and in the bulk organic phase at approximately the same rates, that olefinic compounds are effective inhibitors of the ozone-mediated oxidation reaction, and that the rate of the oxidation is proportional to the fraction of ozone molecules that do not react with the olefinic compounds.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the reactions of ozone with unsaturated fatty acids and proteins that are solubilized in reverse micellar systems.
the reactions of ozone with unsaturated fatty acids and proteins in reverse micelles and with the effect of fatty acids on the ozonation of proteins in reverse micelle systems.
the reaction of ozone with proteins in reverse micelles, and the effect of unsaturated fatty acids and alkenes on this reaction.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the ozone-mediated oxidation reactions of proteins are inhibited by olefins in reverse micelles, and the extent of inhibition is predictable based on the concentrations of the olefin and the protein and their respective reactivities toward ozone.

the ozone-mediated oxidation reactions of tryptophyl residues and other amino acid residues in the protein are strongly inhibited by the addition of unsaturated fatty acids, which react with ozone at a rate comparable to the reaction rate of the protein.
the rate of reaction with ozone of a given compound is independent of its location within the reverse micelle.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ozonation of proteins in reverse micelles is strongly inhibited by the presence of oleic acid and other olefins.
we found a new way to inhibit the ozone mediated oxidation of proteins and unsaturated lipids in reverse micelles.

we have shown that fatty acid and other unsaturated lipids in the reverse micelle can inhibit ozone-mediated protein oxidation by reacting with ozone at a rate that is competitive with the reaction of ozone with protein.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ozonolysis of proteins in reverse micellar systems is inhibited by unsaturated fatty acids, but that this inhibition is not a function of where the fatty acids reside in the reverse micelle.
the ozonation of tryptophyl residues in proteins is inhibited by unsaturated fatty acids and other olefinic compounds.
the reaction of ozone with unsaturated fatty acids is fast and efficient and that this reaction can be used to protect the proteins against oxidation.
